source_text:
Γράφω δὲ ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἀπὸ Σμύρνης δἰ Ἐφεσίων τῶν ἀξιομακαρίστων. ἔστιν δὲ καὶ ἅμα ἐμοὶ σὺν ἄλλοις πολλοῖς καὶ Κρόκος, τὸ ποθητόν μοι ὄνομα.
περὶ τῶν προελθόντων με ἀπὸ Συρίας εἰς Ῥώμην εἰς δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ πιστεύω ὑμᾶς ἐπεγνωκέναι, οἷς καὶ δηλώσατε ἐγγύς με ὄντα. πάντες γάρ εἰσιν ἄξιοι τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ὑμῶν: οὕς πρέπον ὑμῖν ἐστὶν κατὰ πάντα ἀναπαῦσαι.
ἔγραψα δὲ ὑμῖν ταῦτα τῇ πρὸ ἐννέα καλανδῶν Σεπτεμβρίων. ἔρρωσθε εἰς τέλος ἐν ὑπομονῇ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
thought_title: Closing greetings and travel news from Smyrna
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, telling them he writes from Smyrna and asking them to care for his companions who went ahead to Rome.
pass_a_gloss: I write these things to you from Smyrna through the Ephesians who are worthy of blessing. There is also with me, along with many others, Crocus, the name desired by me. Concerning those who went ahead of me from Syria to Rome for the glory of God, I believe you have come to know them, to whom also make clear that I am near. For all are worthy of God and of you; whom it is fitting for you to refresh in every way. I wrote these things to you on the day before the ninth of the Kalends of September. Farewell to the end in the endurance of Jesus Christ.

choices.why: The compound means 'worthy of being called blessed'; 'blessed' alone would lose the worthiness component.
Keeps the passive participle force of ποθητόν and the dative of agent μοι; 'beloved name' would be too free.
Standard rendering of the purpose phrase; 'to the glory' is also possible but 'for' is clearer for purpose.
The verb means to give rest or refreshment; 'rest' as a transitive verb is awkward in English, so 'refresh' captures the active sense.
Standard epistolary closing formula; 'be strong' would be overly literal and miss the conventional force.

pass_b_english: I am writing this to you from Smyrna, through the Ephesians who are worthy of blessing. Crocus is with me as well, along with many others, and his name is dear to me.

As for those who went ahead of me from Syria to Rome for the glory of God, I trust you have come to know them. Let them know that I am near. They are all worthy of God and of you, and it is fitting for you to refresh them in every way.
I wrote this to you on the ninth day before the Kalends of September. Farewell to the end, in the endurance of Jesus Christ.

last_rejected.why: ποθητόν means 'dearly loved,' not 'longed for'; Crocus is beloved, not merely missed.
last_rejected.ruling: ποθητός ranges from 'beloved' to 'longed for'; 'long for' fits τὸ ποθητόν μοι ὄνομα without changing meaning.

polish.changed: Clarified that Crocus is the one whose name is dear to Ignatius, made the instruction to inform the travelers direct, and kept the Roman date as the source states it.
